children: U.S. President Donald Trump has grown increasingly frustrated with Vice President JD Vance over Vance's post-election commentary blaming the war with Iran for Republicans' midterm losses, straining their relationship at a key moment for 2028 Republican nomination positioning, according to a media report published Wednesday.

Trump initially appeared unfazed by Vance's lengthy social media post critiquing the administration's messaging, telling reporters, "I think it's largely true." But over the past two weeks, the president has complained to aides and allies that Vance failed to affirm the decision to attack Iran was correct, the
reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter.
Trump hinted publicly at his irritation earlier this month, saying the vice president should have "made one other statement."
The political fallout has elevated Secretary of State Marco Rubio's standing, the

reported. Trump has privately praised Rubio as a strong 2028 presidential contender, with allies noting that Rubio has repeatedly called the Iran strike essential for national security. While many Republicans long assumed Vance, a former Ohio senator, would be the automatic 2028 front-runner, Trump has waffled on his vice president throughout his tenure, creating fresh uncertainty about succession.

Vance has minimized any friction, telling Fox News this week there is "no daylight between the president or any other senior member of the administration." He has also said he hasn't decided whether to run in 2028.
Allies say he is genuinely undecided, pointing to his young family—his fourth child was born in July—and his data-driven approach to political decisions, the

Prediction market data reflects the political fallout: on Polymarket, the odds of Vance being out as vice president by Dec. 31 rose by a percentage point Wednesday to 3.5% but remain low, while on Kalshi, his odds of winning the 2028 presidential election remain near lows at 13%—behind Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff at 17% and ahead of Rubio at 8.8%.

The war's unpopularity could prove decisive. Vance allies reportedly say resumption of major combat operations would reduce his chances of running. After major GOP midterm losses, Vance attempted to separate himself from administration policy, writing, "The reason we lost is the war."
Trump soon responded by stripping Vance of his role in Iran peace talks, reassigning him to investigate alleged fraud in Democratic-run jurisdictions, the
On Wednesday, Vance canceled a planned appearance at The New York Times DealBook Summit, citing Washington meetings on tech outages.
